title: SpaceX conducts 13th Starship test flight
summary: SpaceX launched its 13th suborbital test flight of Starship on July 24, marking a milestone by deploying functioning satellites for the first time. The test aimed to address issues from the previous flight.

title: ULA deals with financial challenges caused by Vulcan grounding
summary: ULA's corporate parents have guaranteed a loan to address financial challenges stemming from the grounding of its Vulcan Centaur rocket. The company is facing difficulties due to the rocket's temporary halt in operations.

title: LatConnect 60 Unveils Proprietary AI Capabilities Following Growing Indo-Pacific Defence Interest in SWIRSAT
summary: LatConnect 60 introduced proprietary AI capabilities for its Earth observation satellites, responding to increased defense interest in the Indo-Pacific region, particularly for SWIRSAT.

title: Office of Space Commerce to move ahead on mission authorization
summary: The Commerce Department is advancing plans for a voluntary mission authorization system to regulate novel space activities not covered by other agencies. This initiative aims to fill regulatory gaps in emerging space operations.

title: Lightning strikes Long March 3B after liftoff, Kinetica-1 launches 5 satellites
summary: A Long March 3B rocket successfully delivered its payload to orbit despite being struck by lightning shortly after liftoff. Separately, the Kinetica-1 launch carried five satellites into space.
company: China Aerospace Science and Technology Corporation (CASC)

title: EU delays release of Copernicus imagery over Gulf of Oman
summary: The European Union delayed the release of certain Copernicus Sentinel-1 and Sentinel-2 imagery for 24 hours due to a request from the United States. The delay was prompted by concerns over the Gulf of Oman region.

title: Air Force takes over troubled military GPS receiver program
summary: The Air Force Life Cycle Management Center will now oversee the development, integration, and sustainment of military GPS receiver equipment. This move aims to address issues with accessing the military’s encrypted GPS signal.
company: Air Force Life Cycle Management Center

title: NASA programs feel effects of workforce reductions
summary: NASA reports that over two dozen major projects have been impacted by a 20% reduction in its civil servant workforce over the past year. The workforce cuts are affecting critical programs across the agency.

title: Poland commits $745 million to EU’s IRIS² constellation project
summary: Poland has committed $745 million to the EU's IRIS² multi-orbit satellite internet constellation project. The investment aims to support the development of the constellation.

title: Mark Matossian co-founds Whipsmart Ventures to fund space and deep tech
summary: Mark Matossian has co-founded Whipsmart Ventures, a venture capital fund aimed at investing in space and deep tech startups. The fund is established in collaboration with a software engineer and a best-selling author.

title: SpaceX's Starship megarocket makes the 'softest splashdown' ever after launching next-gen Starlink satellites in Flight 13 test (video)
summary: SpaceX successfully launched its Starship megarocket on its 13th test flight, deploying next-gen Starlink satellites and achieving the 'softest splashdown' ever. The flight marked a significant milestone with a surprising successful conclusion.

title: ZWO Seestar S30 Pro smart telescope review
summary: The ZWO Seestar S30 Pro is a compact, automated smart telescope featuring a higher resolution upgrade. This review highlights its advanced capabilities and design improvements.

title: We boldly chat with 'Star Trek: Strange New Worlds' showrunners about space dinosaurs and Lovecraftian horrors for season 4 (interview)
summary: The showrunners of 'Star Trek: Strange New Worlds' discuss incorporating space dinosaurs and Lovecraftian horrors into season 4. They express enthusiasm about integrating dinosaurs into the show's narrative.

title: What lurks beneath the volcanoes of Jupiter's moon Io? NASA's Juno probe just took a peek
summary: NASA's Juno probe has provided new insights into the subsurface of Jupiter's moon Io, revealing volcanic activity that could change how scientists study volcanoes across the solar system. The findings may also have implications for understanding volcanic processes on Earth.

title: Planet hunter gets the silent treatment | Space photo of the day for July 24, 2026
summary: ESA's Plato spacecraft has completed critical testing ahead of its upcoming spaceflight. The mission aims to hunt for Earth-like exoplanets.

title: Lightning strike on Chinese rocket captured in epic launch photo
summary: A Chinese Long March-3B rocket was struck by lightning shortly after liftoff, yet the launch successfully deployed its satellite payload into orbit.

title: This Week In Space LIVE: The Viking Mars landings 50 years later
summary: A live event titled 'This Week In Space' is airing on July 24 to commemorate the 50th anniversary of the Viking Mars landings. The broadcast will discuss the historical significance of these missions.

title: Hubble telescope watches unique nova explosion fire cosmic 'bullets' through the Milky Way at 20 million mph
summary: Astronomers using the Hubble telescope observed a unique helium nova explosion in the Milky Way, which is ejecting cosmic 'bullets' at speeds of 20 million mph. This is the only known instance of such an event in our galaxy.

title: Vulcan Centaur swapped out again: NASA goes with SpaceX Falcon Heavy rocket for launch of space weather mission
summary: NASA's SunRISE mission will now launch on a SpaceX Falcon Heavy rocket instead of ULA's Vulcan Centaur. The change in launch vehicle was announced after Vulcan Centaur faced delays.

title: NASA’s ESCAPADE Snaps Family Portrait of Earth, Moon
summary: NASA's ESCAPADE spacecraft captured images of Earth and the Moon from deep space. The photos were taken in visible and thermal infrared light during its journey to Mars.

title: New Crew Members Welcomed to International Space Station
summary: Three new crew members—Anna Kikina and Pyotr Dubrov of Roscosmos, and Anil Menon of NASA—arrived at the International Space Station on July 14, 2026. They were welcomed aboard the station and celebrated their arrival with a cake.

title: NASA Announces New Spacecraft Technology Demonstration Mission at Moon
summary: NASA has announced a new spacecraft technology demonstration mission at the Moon, partnering with industry to advance cislunar infrastructure for the Artemis program. The CAPSTONE 02 mission, awarded to Advanced Space, will test rendezvous, autonomous navigation, and communication capabilities.

title: NASA to Support Blue Origin New Glenn Rocket Testing, Advance Artemis
summary: NASA and Blue Origin agreed to conduct second stage hot fire testing for the New Glenn rocket at Stennis Space Center. This collaboration supports NASA's Artemis program and involves a reimbursable Space Act Agreement.

title: Hubble Spies One-Sided Spiral
summary: The Hubble Space Telescope captured an image of the spiral galaxy NGC 4654, which is located 72 million light-years away in the constellation Virgo. The galaxy's asymmetric structure is highlighted in the observation.

title: A Million-Panel Project
summary: Utah has inaugurated a massive solar power and battery storage facility, featuring a million panels. The project is one of the largest in the region.

title: Curiosity Blog, Sols 4954–4960: Celebrating Our Rover Engineers Past and Present
summary: The Curiosity rover team celebrates the contributions of past and present engineers in a recent blog post. The post highlights the APXS instrument's role in measuring rock chemistry during operations.

title: Look for NASA+ Now Streaming on Amazon Fire TV
summary: NASA's streaming service, NASA+, is now available on Amazon Fire TV Channels, expanding access to space content via Alexa. Future programming may include science mission launches and test flights.

title: Crews Move Artemis IV Liquid Hydrogen Tank
summary: NASA crews moved the 130-foot-tall liquid hydrogen tank for Artemis IV from Michoud Assembly Facility to a test building on May 15, 2026. The tank will be part of the core stage for the Artemis IV mission.

title: NASA’s MAVEN Illuminates New Understanding of Auroras at Mars
summary: NASA's MAVEN mission has revealed that auroras on Mars form similarly to those on Earth, with new findings published in Nature Communications. This discovery helps solve a key puzzle in understanding Martian atmospheric phenomena.

title: Blue Origin to conduct New Glenn second stage hot fires on Stennis B-2 stand
summary: NASA and Blue Origin have finalized plans to conduct hot-fire tests for the second stage of Blue Origin's New Glenn rocket at the Stennis B-2 test stand. This marks a significant step in the development and preparation of the New Glenn rocket for future missions.

title: Starship Flight 13 achieves new firsts for SpaceX
summary: Starship Flight 13, featuring Booster 20 and Ship 40, achieved new milestones for SpaceX on its third attempt. This marks another step forward in SpaceX's development of the Starship program.

title: Soyuz MS-29 crew arrives at ISS, U.S. EVA completes Canadarm2 repairs
summary: The Soyuz MS-29 crew successfully arrived at the International Space Station (ISS), increasing the station's crew size. A U.S. extravehicular activity (EVA) completed repairs on the Canadarm2 robotic arm.

title: Path to Starship Flight 13 requires additional Booster 20 test
summary: SpaceX is preparing for Starship Flight 13, targeting a launch no earlier than July 23, but requires additional testing of Booster 20. The delay highlights ongoing technical challenges in the Starship program.

title: Falcon 9 to launch MRV-1 robotic servicing spacecraft for Northrop Grumman
summary: SpaceX's Falcon 9 is scheduled to launch the MRV-1 robotic servicing spacecraft for Northrop Grumman from Florida. This mission aims to demonstrate in-space servicing capabilities.

title: Launch Preview: Falcon 9, Starship, and Chinese rockets scheduled to launch
summary: SpaceX is preparing for a new launch attempt of Starship Flight 13 after the previous attempt was aborted. Additionally, Falcon 9 and Chinese rockets are also scheduled for launches.

title: Making Progress: Relativity’s Terran R, Rocket Lab’s Neutron, and PLD Space’s Miura 5
summary: Three companies—Relativity Space, Rocket Lab, and PLD Space—are making progress on their respective medium-lift launch vehicles: Terran R, Neutron, and Miura 5. While SpaceX's Starship has dominated recent headlines, these competitors are advancing their own reusable rocket programs.

title: China’s first recovered booster returns to port as LandSpace aims for first land recovery
summary: China achieved a milestone with the first successful recovery of a booster, and LandSpace is now aiming for the first land recovery of its booster.

title: Soyuz MS-29 launches new crew to ISS from Baikonur
summary: The Soyuz MS-29 spacecraft successfully launched a new crew to the International Space Station (ISS) from the Baikonur Cosmodrome on July 14. This marks another mission to maintain the orbital laboratory's operations.

title: Launch Preview: Soyuz to launch crew to ISS, Starship to fly another test flight
summary: Soyuz is set to launch a crew to the International Space Station (ISS), while SpaceX's Starship is preparing for its 13th flight test. Seven launches are scheduled globally this week.

title: TEC Business to Business website
summary: The news source is a B2B website focused on the technology, electronics, and computing industries. No specific space industry news is provided in the given text.

title: ESA Delivers: 50 years booklet
summary: ESA celebrates 50 years with a booklet highlighting 50 key achievements. The publication marks five decades of milestones in the European space sector.

title: The silicon brains steering next-generation antennas
summary: Next-generation antennas are being enhanced with advanced silicon-based technologies for improved performance. These innovations are critical for advancing communication and radar systems in the space industry.

title: Plato's electronics ready for space
summary: ESA's PLATO spacecraft has completed key electromagnetic compatibility tests in the Maxwell Test Chamber, confirming its electronics are space-ready. The mission is scheduled to launch on an Ariane 6 rocket in March 2027.

title: Test firing at brand new green chemical propulsion lab
summary: A new green chemical propulsion lab conducted its first test firing. This marks a significant step in developing environmentally friendly propulsion technologies for space missions.

title: Upcoming ESA–Industry events on CM25 implementation
summary: ESA is hosting events to discuss the implementation of CM25, the Council Meeting at Ministerial Level 2025, focusing on industrial opportunities and thematic priorities. These events aim to engage the industrial community and provide updates on ESA's planned activities.

title: One robotic arm to rule them all
summary: The article discusses a new robotic arm designed for space applications, highlighting its versatility and potential impact on future missions. The innovation is expected to enhance robotic operations in space exploration and satellite servicing.

title: We’re back: Proba-3 ready for more science
summary: The Proba-3 mission's Coronagraph spacecraft and ASPIICS instrument are fully operational, resuming formation flying to create artificial eclipses for scientific observations.

title: ESA’s Prodex programme brings scientific research to space
summary: ESA's Prodex programme enables European research institutes to participate in space science missions. The latest success is the 4DSpace-Daedalus mission launch in Norway.

title: ESA Puts €65M Behind Europe’s First Lunar Ice Rover
summary: ESA has committed €65 million to Europe's first lunar polar ice exploration rover mission, led by ispace-Europe. This marks a significant step for Europe's involvement in lunar exploration.

title: Lunar Outpost Plans to Fly NVIDIA Chips to the Moon
summary: Lunar Outpost is planning to send NVIDIA chips to the Moon, merging the semiconductor industry with lunar exploration efforts. This initiative highlights the growing intersection of technology and space missions.

title: FCC Filings Show Eutelsat is Working on a New 528-sat Constellation Beyond OneWeb
summary: FCC filings indicate Eutelsat is developing a new constellation of 528 satellites, separate from its OneWeb program. The company suggests the 'Next' program is not yet fully developed.

title: NASA Puts $2B Price Tag on Nuclear Mars Mission
summary: NASA has estimated a $2 billion cost for the Space Reactor-1 Freedom, a fission-powered spacecraft designed for interplanetary missions to Mars. This marks the first such mission to utilize nuclear propulsion technology.

title: Intel Authorization Act Proposes Limiting Commercial EO Access
summary: The proposed Intel Authorization Act seeks to restrict commercial Earth observation (EO) satellite operators from sharing certain data with the public. The U.S. government argues that EO data access is a privilege, not a right.

title: The UK Scraps the Department in Charge of UKSA
summary: The UK has decided to abolish the department overseeing the UK Space Agency (UKSA) as highlighted during the Farnborough Air Show. This move comes as the new Prime Minister Andy Burnham seeks to restructure government departments.

title: The UK and Space Florida Launch Joint Fund
summary: The UK and Space Florida have launched a joint fund to support projects with partners from both regions. This initiative aims to foster collaboration between the two entities in the space industry.

title: Breaking Down the $686B Space Economy
summary: The global space economy reached a record $686 billion in 2025, according to the Space Foundation. This marks significant growth in the industry.

title: FCC Eyes Wi-Fi and Bluetooth Bands for Satellites
summary: The FCC is considering a proposal to permit unlicensed wireless devices to communicate directly with satellites using Wi-Fi and Bluetooth bands. This move aims to expand satellite connectivity options for consumer devices.

title: deltaVision Raises €10.2M to Build In-Orbit Refueling Tech
summary: deltaVision has raised €10.2 million to develop in-orbit refueling technology. The funds will be used to expand manufacturing capacity and research new capabilities.

title: NASA to Support New Glenn Hot Fire Testing at Stennis Space Center
summary: NASA and Blue Origin will collaborate on second stage hot fire testing for the New Glenn rocket at NASA's Stennis Space Center in Mississippi. This partnership aims to advance the development of the New Glenn rocket.

title: Two Galileo Satellites Enter Service for Europe
summary: Two new Galileo satellites, SAT 33 and SAT 34, have entered service, enhancing Europe's satellite navigation system. The European Space Agency (ESA) announced their operational status, boosting the system's capability and resilience.

title: Telco CEOs Shut Down the Idea of Satellite MVNO, Say LEO Isn’t a Threat to Broadband
summary: Top telco CEOs rejected the idea of forming a satellite MVNO agreement, stating they do not view LEO satellite broadband as a significant competitive threat to their services.

title: Space Is Coming for Silicon
summary: SpaceX has introduced Starmind, an AI satellite megaconstellation, marking a significant step in orbital data centers. Elon Musk highlighted the project as part of SpaceX's expanding space-based infrastructure.

title: Iceye and KT SAT Partner on Flood Intelligence in South Korea
summary: Iceye and KT SAT have formed a strategic partnership to provide flood monitoring solutions in South Korea for government and commercial entities. This collaboration represents the first deployment of Iceye's solutions in the region.

title: Intellian Releases New Terminal for Iridium GMDSS Service
summary: Intellian has launched a new terminal for Iridium's GMDSS maritime safety service, leveraging the Iridium Certus 100 service. The terminal was announced on Thursday and is designed for use with the Global Maritime Distress and Safety System.

title: Frequency Electronics Reports Increased Demand From Proliferated Satellite Programs
summary: Frequency Electronics reported $18 million in recent contract wins, including an $11 million award from an undisclosed major aerospace prime contractor for a proliferated satellite program.

title: FCC Approves a New C-Band Auction
summary: The FCC approved a new C-band auction to clear 160 megahertz of the upper C-band spectrum, building on previous efforts. This auction aims to further allocate spectrum for wireless services.

title: Lite Coms Wins $22M Contract to Support Operational Readiness
summary: Lite Coms secured a $22 million contract from an unnamed government and defense customer to supply satellite communications for operational readiness. The company specializes in integration and manufacturing of satellite communication solutions.

title: FCC Overhauls Satellite Licensing, Adopts ‘Assembly Line’ Approach
summary: The FCC approved a major overhaul of its satellite and earth station licensing process to implement a streamlined 'licensing assembly line' approach. This change aims to simplify and expedite the approval process for space industry stakeholders.
